purpose: Attach the proven OneSend/QR reporter chain to the PR249 kernel so one boot shows how far arm_vm_init gets, with the ADT identity fix in place

why_not_ramoops.observation: The kernel has ramoops enabled but writes no log.
why_not_ramoops.cause: 0004-tb710fu-ramoops-console.patch calls tb710fu_ramoops_init() after arm_vm_init() returns (arm_init: arm_vm_init(...) then tb710fu_ramoops_init()). Before that, tb710fu_ramoops_putc() only appends to a 4096-byte RAM buffer called `early`; nothing touches the persistent zone. The stop is inside arm_vm_init, so init never runs and the zone is never written.
why_not_ramoops.conclusion: Empty pstore is expected here and is not evidence about where the kernel stopped.

fidelity_regression.note: Re-running the widened tool on cc690c9a must reproduce the historical reporter byte for byte

expected_reading.last_line_means: The last checkpoint text/QR is the last place the reporter ran; it is a boundary, not a fault PC
expected_reading.if_it_reaches_set_mmu_ttb_alternate: arm_vm_init completed every traced call, so the stop is at or after the TTBR1 switch
expected_reading.if_it_stops_earlier: The named call is the first one that did not return, which separates the stages inside arm_vm_init
expected_reading.no_export_pause: This build continues the original call sequence; it does not intentionally pause before the switch
expected_reading.scan: Use OneSend to scan the on-screen QR; the report continues rotating while the kernel runs

boundary: This is a diagnostic image, not a functional fix and not hardware acceptance.
The reporter appends an 835,584 B segment and rewrites 24 BL sites; layout perturbation is expected and must be accounted for when comparing with the clean kernel.
ADT identity is included but its effect on the stop point is still unproven.
No device flash, reboot or partition operation was performed by the agent.
